instruction: Look at chamfer_plate.step in SOLIDWORKS with the SOLIDWORKS CAM add-in. For the steps below, start SOLIDWORKS 2025 from the desktop shortcut and use its installed SOLIDWORKS CAM/CAMWorks add-in; there is no separate SolidCAM desktop program in this image. Use an installed chamfer mill to create standard 2.5D Chamfer operations on the top outside contour and all four hole mouths of chamfer_plate.step. The chamfer toolpath must cover the outside contour and every hole opening. Use the standard Chamfer operation and keep SOLIDWORKS CAM's default generated NC comments; do not rename operations just to add labels. Do not force exact tool station numbers, spindle speeds, feedrates, or internal tool-library IDs if SOLIDWORKS CAM's Technology Database assigns stable defaults; use suitable installed tool-library entries for the required operation types and let the posted NC program reflect those real CAM selections. Save the required output file(s) to the Desktop: C:\Users\User\Desktop\task-5.nc. Generate the required NC/G-code file(s) by using SOLIDWORKS CAM's normal Post Process workflow after calculating the toolpath, with an installed .ctl postprocessor from C:\ProgramData\SOLIDWORKS\SOLIDWORKS CAM 2025\Posts. For milling tasks, prefer m3axis-tutorial.ctl, mach_iii.ctl, or haas_vf3.ctl; for turning tasks, use an installed turning .ctl post such as fanuc_t2axis.ctl. If the generated program opens in NC Editor or is initially saved with a different extension, use Save As from that generated program to save the exact requested Desktop filename(s).
